1.0.0.en: The book declares that Moses was "the servant of the Lord" so that the people would not regard him as a god because of his greatness. Likewise it calls Joshua "Moses' minister", and this is for two reasons:

1.0.1.en: 1- The humility of Joshua, the writer of the book, who does not call himself the head or the leader; this protects him from pride.

1.0.2.en: 2- A declaration that he is bound by all the teachings of God which were delivered to Moses, so that he is Moses' natural continuation. These verses show the role of God in the people's receiving of their inheritance, which points to the salvation of mankind and their receiving of their heavenly portion. Moses points to the Law, which does not bring mankind to heaven but promises them that, and then hands the leadership over to Joshua, who is a symbol of Christ, who gives us eternal life.

1.1.0.en: The servant dies, but the service continues, and someone is urgently needed to lead it after Moses. The divine command comes to Joshua, who was still affected by the death of Moses, to take up the leadership, and to do so immediately, "now", at the time when the Jordan was in its season of flooding (the time of harvest) (ch. 3:15, 16). How could Joshua cross with all the people, their women, their children and their belongings, a flooded and violently flowing river, with no crossing (bridge) or boats for passage?!

1.1.1.en: The name Jordan means "descender", since its rate of descent equals 30 times the descent of the Nile, which makes the crossing even harder; yet the promise of the Lord to His people must be fulfilled.

1.2.0.en: Now God fulfills His promise to Moses to give the people the Promised Land (Num 13:1, Deut 11:24), and also fulfills His promises to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. God promises His people that every place that the sole of their foot shall tread upon will be theirs, and this means:

1.2.1.en: 1- The unlimited love of God for His people, that they may take as much of the land as they are able.

1.2.2.en: 2- The importance of spiritual striving for obtaining the grace of God.

1.2.3.en: 3- It signifies the spiritual man who treads upon earthly desires as much as he is able, and so receives countless heavenly blessings.

1.2.4.en: God says in the past tense, "have I given unto you", although they did not yet possess it, because it is in the heart of God to give it to them, and so it is a settled matter that must come to pass; that is, God's promise to them is sure.

1.3.1.en: The Hittites: they are the sons of Heth, son of Canaan, son of Ham (Gen 10:15), and they represent the strongest of the Canaanite peoples. Their country extended through Palestine, northern Syria, northern Iraq and Asia Minor, that is, Turkey. The children of Israel took possession of some of their lands but did not possess the rest, because of their negligence in carrying out God's commandments to drive out the wicked and cleanse the land. The Hittites fought many wars with Egypt, the strongest nation at that time.

1.3.2.en: The Lord shows the borders of the land: the Arabian desert and the wilderness of Sinai to the south, Lebanon to the north, the river Euphrates, which is 2,850 kilometers long, to the east, and the Mediterranean Sea to the west. Thus the wilderness, which signifies spiritual drought, and the world with its salt water, which the Mediterranean Sea signifies, remain outside the borders. This area includes the land of the Hittites and other Canaanites. The Hittites were mentioned specifically because they were the strongest of the peoples in this region, to support His people and to confirm their faith and their ability to possess the Promised Land, even the regions in which the strong peoples dwell.

1.4.0.en: He promises Joshua that none of these pagan peoples, whose land they were entering to possess, would be able to stand before him; rather, all would submit to him, and he would defeat them and drive them out. Just as God supported Moses, so He supports Joshua.

1.5.0.en: God also encouraged Joshua that he would possess this land which he was entering and divide it among the tribes of the children of Israel, as He promised the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

1.5.1.en: God is the One who takes the initiative to push us along the way of our salvation with support, encouragement and companionship. So do not fear failure and do not turn back, but complete the way by His strength.

1.6.0.en: Only: all you have to do is ...

1.6.1.en: To the right hand or to the left: the right signifies excess and exaggeration, and the left signifies neglect, deficiency and carelessness. Prosper: succeed.

1.6.2.en: God tells Joshua, as a servant responsible for leading his people, that his duty is to be steadfast in faith and courageous, however strong the enemies who face him. What is required of him is not any material strength but holding fast, with all exactness, to the law of God which Moses taught him, and so he will be assured of success in his wars and in all his works.

1.7.0.en: Meditate: keep the words and repeat them so that they remain in your mind.

1.7.1.en: He stresses to him the importance of holding fast to the word of God, so that he understands it, keeps it and repeats it throughout the day and even in the night, and does not turn aside from it, and then it corrects his errors and makes him succeed in all his life.

1.8.0.en: Because of the difficulty of confronting the many nations dwelling in the land of Canaan, God encourages Joshua for the third time and supports him, so that he would not fear their strength but rely on the command of God and His promise to be with him.

1.8.1.en: Take care to read the word of God, to meditate on it, to memorize it and to repeat it throughout your day in the form of a verse or a psalm, so that you may feel the presence of God with you and rely on Him, and even delight in fellowship with Him. Then you will rejoice even in the midst of difficult circumstances and pass through them reassured, because God is with you.

1.9.0.en: Officers: the civil leaders of the children of Israel.

1.9.1.en: Host: the place where they pitch their tents and dwell.

1.9.2.en: Joshua commanded the officers of the people to pass through the midst of them to alert them, to have them prepare to enter the Promised Land, and to prepare the food and drink needed for this long journey, whose extent was not known, because they were entering among people who were strangers to them, whom they would fight and drive out of their land because of their wickedness. This provision they took from the plants and produce of the land east of the Jordan, where the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh dwelt. Here appears the importance of human spiritual striving, which is supported by divine grace: they do what they are able to do by taking provision, and God completes His grace by their victory over the enemies.

1.9.3.en: Do everything you are able to do to show your love for God by holding fast to your prayers, your readings and your service of others; and on the other hand, avoid the sources of evil and keep away from every sin, and God will support you and make you prosper in all your ways.

1.10.0.en: Beyond Jordan toward the sunrising: the eastern bank of the river Jordan.

1.10.1.en: Joshua reminded the men of the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh of the command of Moses to them: that after they possessed their land east of the Jordan and built houses for their wives and children and folds for their livestock, they were to go forward before their brethren to fight the enemies and drive them out of their land west of the Jordan, and then, after the war was completed and all the tribes had possessed the new land and settled in it, they would return to their places east of the Jordan (Num 32).

1.11.0.en: The tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh agreed to the commands Joshua gave them, and they also promised to obey him in everything as they had obeyed Moses. The third thing they promised was their readiness to punish with death anyone who disobeyed his words, so that they would not trouble him in his leading of them and in confronting the enemies. And the fourth thing is that they encouraged him to carry out his duties of leadership.

2.0.s.en: (1) The two spies in the house of Rahab

2.0.0.en: Shittim: plural of shittah, that is, the acacia tree; it is the name of a place that was full of acacia trees, located in the land of Moab east of the river Jordan near where it meets the Dead Sea, where the people were staying (Num 25:1). Rahab: a woman's name meaning a broad or wide place.

2.0.1.en: Jericho: it means "fragrance"; it is the name of a city that had an abundance of balsam plants that gave it a sweet fragrance. It is located west of the river Jordan opposite Shittim, about five miles from the river and about 17 miles north-east of Jerusalem. It is a fortified city in a valley and surrounded by fertile land (Map 1). Lebanon Mediterranean Sea Syria Hazor Sea of Galilee Mount Ebal Mount Gerizim Shechem Jordan River Jordan Shiloh Ai Gilgal Gibeon Shittim Jericho Valley of Aijalon Jerusalem Hebron Dead Sea Moab Map (1) In complete secrecy, Joshua sent two spies to study the nature of the land, the site, and the city of Jericho and its fortifications, because it was the first city that Joshua would fight in the Promised Land. Secrecy was necessary to preserve the lives of the two spies. Spying was a necessity before fighting any city.

2.0.2.en: Jericho lies at the entrance of passes between the mountains that lead to the surrounding lands such as Ai and Jerusalem. Joshua, by God's guidance, chose to enter at Jericho and did not enter from the south of Palestine, because the land there is fortified, and so that none of the surrounding nations, such as Egypt and the land of the Arabs, would attack him. Had they entered from the south, Egypt might have risen to resist the attackers, because the south of Palestine is east of the wilderness of Sinai, which belonged to Egypt.

2.0.3.en: It is likely that Rahab rented out her house, part of which she lived in with her family, as an inn for strangers. She also worked in one of the pagan temples as a harlot, since fornication was one of the practices of pagan worship to which Rahab had vowed herself; therefore the temples had male and female prostitutes so that the worshippers might fulfill their vows with them by fornication. This shows us how corrupt the Canaanite pagan worship was at that time, which led God to issue His command to kill many of these corrupt pagans, who deserved death because of the multitude of their evils, and for fear that their bad customs would pass to the Jewish people if they mingled with them.

2.0.4.en: The two spies lodged at Rahab's inn so that none of the inhabitants of Jericho would suspect them, since many people frequented this house for fornication or lodging.

2.0.5.en: The two spies symbolize the apostles of Christ in the sending out of the Twelve and then the sending out of the Seventy, or the disciples sent out two by two to preach.

2.1.0.en: The men told the king of Jericho what had happened, especially since the city was tense and awaiting an attack on it by the Jews, and it was easy to detect the entry of strangers into a limited city like Jericho. The king of Jericho symbolizes the man who resists God.

2.2.0.en: The king asked Rahab to hand over the two men, but she was not willing; rather, she denied that she knew they were Jewish spies, although it will become clear from the rest of the account that she was lying. Lying is approved by Rahab's religion, but it is not approved by Christianity, whatever its reason. Rahab lied because she had heard of the power of the God of the children of Israel and had begun to believe in Him, and she desired to please Him and to take refuge in Him.

2.3.0.en: Rahab misled the king's messengers, telling them that the two men had left before dark, because the gates of Jericho were shut at nightfall like all cities, and that she did not know where they had gone, so the messengers hurried away to search for them as Rahab had instructed them.

2.4.0.en: Laid in order: placed one upon another in an arrangement.

2.4.1.en: After that she brought them up to the roof of her house, where she had laid some stalks of flax to dry after washing, so that they could be combed and turned into threads for weaving, and she hid the two spies under the stalks of flax.

2.4.2.en: Perhaps the flax under which the two spies hid, from which the priestly garments were made in the law of Moses, points to the intercession and work of the priesthood, which hides us in the blessing of the Holy Sacraments, so that we escape the pursuit of Satan.

2.5.0.en: The fords: plural of ford, which is a shallow place where people cross the river by wading through the water on foot.

2.5.1.en: The guards went toward the fords of the Jordan, thinking that the two spies would cross the river there to return to Joshua. And since the city gate was shut as every day, it would be easy to catch the two spies if they were still inside the city.

2.5.2.en: The love of God is wonderful in His protection of the two spies, not through friends of theirs, but through a woman of a foreign race and notorious for evil. So do not be troubled, for you are in a faithful hand, the hand of God, which protects you wherever you go and gives you favor in the eyes of those from whom you do not expect it.

2.6.0.en: Sea of Suph: the Red Sea.

2.6.2.en: After that Rahab told the two spies that she knew that the God of the children of Israel was mighty and would give them the land of the Canaanites, so that everyone was in terror, especially from knowing of the miracle of the Lord's dividing of the Red Sea by the hand of Moses and the drowning of Pharaoh, and then of their victory over the two kings of the Amorites on the way and their killing of them (Deut 2, 3). Rahab had learned these reports through the trade caravans and travelers, especially since she hosted strangers to stay in her house, so that much news of the world around her reached her. What Rahab said declares her faith in God, the God of Israel, as the New Testament testifies to this in (Heb 11:31, Jas 2:25).

2.6.3.en: If the people of God perished in the wilderness through their unbelief in Him and their disobedience to Him in entering the Promised Land, yet Rahab, the Gentile harlot, when she believed in God, prophesied of the children of Israel's taking possession of the land, and God saved her and her household from death, and she even became a grandmother of Christ. So believe in God so that you may enjoy His work in you. Seek Him earnestly, confident of His love, whatever the adverse circumstances around you and whatever your weakness or your sins.

2.7.1.en: Rahab confessed her faith in the one God, the King of heaven and earth, and asked them to deal kindly with her and to confirm that by swearing by the name of the Lord, in return for her kindness to them. This would be by giving her a sign or proposing a plan so that she and all her family would escape death when the people arrived at the city and conquered it.

2.8.0.en: The two men assured her that they were responsible for her life and that of her household, since they would deal kindly with her in return for her hiding them, so that they would not die with the inhabitants of Jericho.

2.9.1.en: Since her house was adjoining the wall of the city, she let them down by a rope through the window of her house, whose wall is the wall of the city, because they could not go out by the closed gates, which were guarded by the king's agents.

2.10.0.en: The pursuers: the king's men whom he sent to run after the two spies and catch them.

2.10.1.en: She told them to go toward the mountains between Jericho and Jerusalem, that is, opposite to the direction of the river Jordan which they had crossed when they came to Jericho, and she told them to hide from those who were searching for them in the mountain for three days, which was the expected length of the search, and then to turn back and cross the Jordan to Joshua.

2.11.1.en: The two spies set a sign for Rahab so that the Jewish attackers would know her house when they attacked Jericho, and it was to hang a scarlet-colored cord in the window of her house adjoining the wall. They commanded her to gather her father, her mother and all her household inside her house so that they would not die, and if she did not fulfill this condition, the attackers would not know her and her family, and they would be exposed to death. Therefore the two spies said to her that we are blameless of our oath to you to preserve the life of you and your family if you do not fulfill this condition.

2.11.2.en: The scarlet color signifies the blood of Christ, which is a condition for obtaining salvation, and the house of Rahab signifies the Church, in which the believers take refuge; for without the Church and its sacraments and the means of grace within it, we do not obtain salvation.

2.12.0.en: The two spies set two conditions for salvation by this sign: the first is the commitment to remain inside the house, because there is no salvation outside the Church, and whoever goes out is responsible for the destruction that befalls him.

2.12.1.en: The second condition is to keep the matter secret from the king, lest he destroy the two spies, and this is an indication of the necessity of our faithfulness to Christ, that we not betray Him, so that He may allow us to enjoy His salvation.

2.13.0.en: Then they departed, and she put the scarlet cord in the window. This shows her faith, which made her hang the scarlet cord after the two spies left her house.

2.14.0.en: The two spies hid in the mountain for three days as she had told them, and then returned to Joshua and told him all that had happened and of the terror of the inhabitants of the land because of the Jewish people, because everyone was certain of the power of the God of the children of Israel.

2.14.1.en: The words of the two spies show their strong faith in the power of God, who would give them the land of Canaan, for they said, "Truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land"; and this is the opposite of the ten spies in their unbelief long ago in the days of Moses, because of which all the people died in the wilderness of Sinai and did not enter the Promised Land.

2.14.2.en: Although the two spies relied on God's protection of them, they acted with wisdom and hid for three days. May you be faithful in performing your duties and act with wisdom in every situation, according to what God guides you and those who love you advise you, and so enjoy God's care; for He does not love the lazy and the negligent, but He keeps and saves the weak and the humble who are faithful in their works.
